title: Water-heater step-response identification
equipment: Electric recirculating water heater, outlet-temperature sensor, and heater power stage
physicalPurpose: Estimate local heater dynamics from a safe input/output recording when physical parameters are unavailable.
principalTechnique: Qualified open-loop step test and FOPDT reaction-curve identification
objective: Design and approve a bounded water-heater step experiment, qualify its measured data, estimate one local dynamic model with explicit resolution limits, and explain why that model still requires independent validation.

simplifications: One local self-regulating response near fixed flow and ambient conditions.
Deterministic simulation data have no added sensor noise; uncertainty still records search resolution and residual evidence.
The fitter cannot read configured truth.
Boiling, flow loss, stratification, efficiency change, sensor dynamics, and actuator faults are omitted.

baseline.limitation: The first-principles derivation depends on physical parameters that may be unavailable or inaccurate on installed equipment.

change.decision: Estimate from immutable time/MV/PV/quality samples only, retain all candidates and uncertainty, and leave the selected preview unaccepted until independent validation.

abortPredicates: PV, requested MV, applied MV, or timestamp is nonfinite
quality is bad or a sample gap exceeds 0.15 s
requested or applied MV leaves 0..100 percent
the input or output is clipped or saturated
an unapproved event changes the operating condition
safety.restorationMode: Manual at the reviewed 20 percent operating point, then 0 percent on safety abort
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The simulation experiment approval does not authorise a physical step.
Configured truth, measured simulation data, and the identified preview remain separately labelled.

video.viewerOutcome: Design a safe step test and recover a provenance-correct FOPDT preview without treating fit as validation.

learning.context: The same recirculating heater must be modelled when its thermal capacitance, losses, efficiency, or transport delay are not reliably known.
learning.reason: A bounded input/output experiment can estimate combined local dynamics, but one fitted recording cannot establish independent prediction.
theory: An open-loop step experiment records a stable baseline, changes one applied input, and observes the output without feedback hiding plant dynamics.
Process gain relates settled output change to input change; apparent dead time locates response onset; model time constant locates the 63.2 percent crossing.
Residual and normalized error compare measured and predicted samples, while fresh quality, regular timing, drift, excitation, clipping, and saturation decide whether fitting is eligible.
Configured truth, measured simulation data, and an identified model have distinct provenance; a same-run sample-resolution envelope is not statistical confidence.
learning.workedPrediction: A 20 to 30 percent step has delta-u=10 percent; the prior physical model predicts delta-y about 2 degC, 31.264 degC at 6 s after the step, and 32 degC final, but those values are withheld from fitting.
practicalPreparation: Inspect equipment, purpose, signals, units, sensor, actuator, operating point, quality, timing, limits, safe state, aborts, and evidence source.
Predict response markers, confirm a settled 30 degC and 20 percent baseline, calculate excitation margin, and obtain approval before a fresh immutable recording.
learning.baseline: Retain the first-principles model as provenance-labelled comparison evidence, then hide its parameters from the fitter and establish the stable measured baseline.
learning.change: Write one reviewed Boolean Test authority; let the project own the 20-percent baseline, 30-percent step, and 20-percent restoration; retain 500 active samples; then qualify the immutable data and fit five supported low-order candidates in project-owned evidence.
learning.comparison: Overlay measured and predicted outlet temperature, locate the gain, delay, and time-constant construction, compare candidate complexity and normalized residual error, then compare the selected preview with configured truth without merging provenance.
learning.validation: Require qualified data and declared parameter tolerances, expose uncertainty and warnings, and leave the result in validation-required state.
learning.explanation: Explain every parameter from the recorded curve and why fitting the same curve cannot demonstrate independent predictive validity.
learning.transfer: For another self-regulating plant, stabilize, bound, approve, record, qualify, fit competing structures, expose uncertainty, restore safely, and reserve different data for validation.
